overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers, compiled in October 1945, identifying two 1943 records concerning the possible postwar return of Formosa (Taiwan) to China and the activities of the Formosan Revolutionists League. The entries refer respectively to information associated with Secretary of State Cordell Hull and to a telegram from the U.S. Embassy at Chungking enclosing an embassy officer’s memorandum on the League, while directing researchers to related decimal-file material.

people.name: George Atcheson Jr.
people.role: U.S. diplomat at the Embassy in China; associated with telegram no. 1484 from Chungking

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Formosa and China
subfiles.about: This filing sheet lists two 1943 records about Formosa’s possible return to China and the Formosan Revolutionists League.
subfiles.summary: The first entry records information dated March 27, 1943, associated with Secretary Hull, concerning the possibility that Formosa would be returned to China after the war, and directs the reader to another decimal-file reference. The second identifies telegram no. 1484 from Chungking, dated August 18, 1943 and associated with George Atcheson Jr., which enclosed an embassy officer’s memorandum on the Formosan Revolutionists League. The sheet was prepared or stamped on October 11, 1945.

interest: This sheet is useful as a documentary roadmap to otherwise dispersed State Department records on wartime planning for Taiwan’s postwar status. It links high-level consideration of returning Formosa to China with American diplomatic reporting on Formosan anti-Japanese revolutionaries, showing that territorial policy and local political movements were treated as connected subjects. Its cross-references may help historians reconstruct missing or separately filed documents.
